notes.title: Ali Aslanbayli
notes.summary: AI engineer building agents, retrieval systems, developer tools, and reliable information workflows.
notes.body:
AI writes code. Engineers build software.

## Background

I got my Master's in Computer Engineering from New York University and a Bachelor's in Computer Science from the University of South Florida.

## Focus

Currently focused on AI systems, retrieval workflows, and developer tools that make complex software easier to reason about. My work tends to sit close to model orchestration, data flow, observability, interfaces, and the infrastructure needed to make AI products reliable.

## Outside of Work

Outside of work I actively train Mixed Martial Arts, enjoy cooking, go on hikes, and am into aquarium fish and reptiles.

## Current Threads

- Experienced in: RAG Systems.
- Building: FireLens.
- Learning: Mojo.
- Interested in: LLM Inference.

notes.title: Professional Experience
notes.summary: Experience building AI systems, retrieval workflows, and developer tools.
notes.body:
## AI Engineer
Providge Consulting | New York, NY | July 2026 - Present

- Engineered multimodal document-understanding systems that extract and reason over complex PDFs containing tables, charts, forms, and scanned images using vision-language models and OCR pipelines.
- Developed autonomous AI agents that dynamically plan multi-step workflows, select specialized tools, and synthesize information from heterogeneous enterprise data sources.
- Designed scalable document-processing pipelines with layout analysis, metadata extraction, and asynchronous orchestration for high-throughput enterprise AI applications.

## GenAI Developer
NYU Research Technology Services | New York, NY | December 2024 - May 2026

- Architected and deployed end-to-end Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines using OpenWebUI and vector databases, improving model accuracy and reducing hallucinations for domain-specific queries.
- Engineered real-time Python data-ingestion modules that integrate Google Search APIs, increasing LLM context coverage by 40% and enabling answers to live-event queries.
- Built a user-facing agentic interface that automates complex data analysis, converting natural language directly into Pandas workflows to accelerate research operations.

notes.title: Agent Swarms Make Model Choice an Architecture Decision
notes.summary: Cursor's swarm experiments are less a case for more agents than a case for better boundaries, memory, and verification.
notes.excerpt: Cursor's swarm experiments are less a case for more agents than a case for better boundaries, memory, and verification.
notes.body:
Cursor's article about agent swarms is easy to read as a story about scale. I think the more useful lesson is quieter: swarms change model selection from a runtime setting into an architectural decision.

## More Agents Do Not Create More Clarity

Parallelism magnifies coordination quality. If responsibilities are vague, more workers create faster ambiguity. If tasks have sharp boundaries and useful handoffs, workers can move independently without losing the larger intent.

When I build agent workflows, I want each step to leave behind an artifact that the next step can inspect: a task brief, a decision record, a patch, a test result, or a concise failure report.

## The Real Unit Is a Verified Outcome

Cheap execution that creates rework is expensive. The useful unit is the cost of a completed, verified outcome: a feature that passes tests, a document workflow that extracts the right fields, or a research answer grounded in the right source material.

Review adds latency and cost, but it is often cheaper than letting a bad assumption propagate through a task tree. Reliable progress is the product.

Related: [[experience]], [[pelmen]].
